findings.title: A single agent session holds the full lethal trifecta: space content, local files and a model-steerable outbound channel
findings.evidence: registerAllTools registers twelve tool collections unconditionally (l.45-73) plus the four migration tools (l.74-107). Capability inventory for the one agent that receives them: (1) PRIVATE DATA - every space, environment, entry, asset, org and taxonomy the CMA token can reach (createToolClient takes `params.spaceId ?? config.spaceId`, utils/tools.ts l.24, so the model names the space, not the operator), plus arbitrary local files through import_space `contentFile`/`config`/`assetsDirectory`. (2) UNTRUSTED INGESTION - get_entry returns the whole entry verbatim (tools/entries/getEntry.ts l.26-28) and search_entries returns entry collections (searchEntries.ts l.124-141); entry text is written by anyone with content-editor access to the space or by upstream integrations, never by the MCP user. (3) OUTBOUND CHANNEL - export_space accepts a model-chosen `host`/`proxy`/`headers` (exportSpace.ts l.99-109), import_space writes content into any space the token reaches (importSpace.ts l.100-119), upload_asset takes an arbitrary `upload` URL (uploadAsset.ts l.13-18), and create_entry/update_entry write attacker-chosen text into a space a third party can read. All three legs sit on the same agent, in the same session, with no separation.
findings.impact: An attacker who can write one entry in a space the token reaches - a CMS is a multi-writer system by design - can plant text that the model reads as instruction and have it act with the operator's full CMA privileges: read every space, publish or delete content, and push what it read to a destination of the attacker's choosing. No flaw needs to be exploited; the capability combination is the flaw.
findings.preconditions: The MCP server is configured with a CMA personal access token, and the model reads content the operator did not author. Both are the documented, intended mode of operation (README.md l.38-39, l.72-73).
findings.recommendation: Break one leg rather than strengthening the prompt. In order of effect: remove the model's control of outbound destinations (F-002); split read tools and write tools into two servers so a session that has ingested space content cannot also mutate or export; drop the ability to name an arbitrary spaceId per call so the blast radius is the configured space rather than the whole token scope; and mark tool results as data (F-003). Document in README.md that the CMA token should be a least-privilege token scoped to the single space in use, since the server cannot enforce that itself.

triage.reason: No allowlist constrains any outbound destination: exportSpace.ts l.99-101 accepts a free-form host and proxy, uploadAsset.ts l.13-18 accepts a free-form URL, and utils/tools.ts l.17-31 builds the client with whatever spaceId the caller passed. There is no mandatory layer between a tool call and the CMA request.

A second principal exists and is named: any Contentful user or integration with write access to an entry in a reachable space authors content that enters the model's context, and is not the MCP operator. The ingesting component is not credential-free either - the same client instance holds the CMA token.

findings.limits: This is a capability inventory over the registered tool set, which is what AI-01 asks for. It does not demonstrate a specific end-to-end exfiltration run; the individual legs are written up separately as F-002 and F-003.
